decision.why: (a) Composer.js passes `on_revised` (usually undefined) into new ComposerMic({...}); View's constructor Object.assign()s it, shadowing ComposerMic.prototype.on_revised, so the in-place clean swap NEVER runs anywhere (AI 2 included) and every send waits await_clean's full 5 s. (b) the ✦ sheet's voice ChatPanel never passes `revise`, so clean_active() is false there regardless of SETTINGS.clean. Fix: Composer forwards the caller's hook as `on_clean`, ComposerMic.on_revised calls it; ChatPanel defaults revise to "clean".
decision.alternative: rename the ComposerMic method instead — rejected, Dictate.js calls this.on_revised by name

decision.why: Servex already emits `delta` events per agent (includePartialMessages). Sessions.js buffers the text of the current reply per role and pushes it on a per-session SSE route /api/session/<id>/stream, full text each time (throttled), plus every line it writes — so a reconnect (the dev-server proxy cuts streams at 30 s) loses nothing and replies land without the 1.5 s poll.
decision.alternative: write deltas into the session jsonl — rejected, bloats the append-only record

Chat.js: `lives` map + follow() lifts live bubbles out and back; chat_line() first line drops the speaker's live bubble; draw() prompt branch drops a sent bubble; new live_bubble()/drop_live() before draw(); new live()/stream() on the returned object. decision.what: (5)+(6) one mechanism: spoken lines are HELD from both assistants until a quiet event
decision.why: The owner's filler complaint came from the fast one answering every 1.5 s chunk. Now Servex holds every voice line (it carries floor + quiet_ms), and releases the whole thought to both assistants when the browser's floor.js reports 2.5 s of silence (or the line arrives already that quiet, or 12 s pass with no event). The fast brief says reply `(listening)` to stay silent; Sessions drops that and short fillers as invisible {skip} lines.
decision.alternative: brief-only fix (tell fast not to say filler) — rejected alone: it still answered mid-thought

log.msg: (4) confirmed live: the growing bubble swaps to the clean-up in place (phone-frames.json 12.0 s: commas -> full stops, 'and then' comma); the say line carries text=clean, raw=Whisper.

findings.text: All six items are covered. (1–2) Dictation now grows as a bubble in the chat log, and the gear can switch it back to the text box: Mic.js `SETTINGS.into`, Chat.js `live()`. (3) Replies stream in over a server-sent-events feed: Sessions.js `streaming()`/`push()`, Chat.js `stream()`. (4) The cause of the raw-Whisper bubbles is found and fixed: an `on_revised` option was hiding ComposerMic's own method (Mic.js `on_revised`, Composer.js `on_clean`), and the ✦ sheet never turned on `revise`, which now defaults to it (ChatPanel.js:361). (5) Filler replies are dropped server-side (Sessions.js `is_filler`) and the fast brief is rewritten to match. (6) floor.js has a real `on_quiet` event, which Servex's hold/release is built on.

The phone-width proof holds up. proof/1-words-growing.png shows a bubble growing mid-dictation, proof/3-reply-streaming.png shows a reply with its caret, and proof/sessions-test.txt shows 15/15 server checks passing. The reply stream in the screenshot comes from a mocked `/stream` route (phone-proof.mjs:37), so the browser and server halves are proven separately, never together end to end.

In proof/1-words-growing.png and phone-frames.json, the whole bubble is grey "guess" at every frame. The ink/grey split (`settled` vs `guess`, Mic.js `show_live`) never shows mid-sentence, so either the split rarely happens in practice or it isn't working. Worth one look with a longer utterance.

A typed line that arrives while spoken lines are still held goes to both assistants at once, ahead of the earlier spoken words (Sessions.js `say`, the `else` branch at diff line 51). The assistants then hear the conversation out of order. Releasing the held lines first, before sending the typed one, would fix it.

A page with no level meter never fires `quiet`, so each spoken line waits the full 12 s `hold_max_ms` before anyone answers (Sessions.js diff line 13). That can feel like the assistants stopped working. Consider a shorter fallback, or releasing on the line's own `floor: "done"` when the page can't measure silence.

The new `/api/session/<id>/stream` sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (Sessions.js `open_stream`). Any website open in the owner's browser could read a session's transcript live if it guesses the short `v-xxxxxxx` id. This matches the existing session routes, but a stream of everything said is a bigger exposure than before.

Moving the `revise: "clean"` default into ChatPanel (ChatPanel.js:361) turns clean-up model calls on for every ChatPanel, including the demo panels in ext/Chat/panel/ and ext/Chat/drill/. It is cheap, but it is a behaviour change beyond the ✦ sheet the owner asked about.
rail.js `stop_quiet` is set once with `??=` and never cleared in `forget_session()`. It stays harmless only because it reads `this.session` fresh on every call.

decision.what: merged with voice-sessions e-fixes (landed on michael/dev meanwhile), which had its own floor: the fast REPLY held while speaking, a /api/session/floor verb releasing it at 1.5 s
decision.why: Both kept, renamed apart: their `held`/`release()` (a held fast reply) and `floor` verb stay; mine became `thoughts`/`hold_thought()`/`release_thought()`. For a spoken line with a floor, the INPUT is now held from both assistants until 2.5 s of quiet (the quiet event), so the fast one never produces a mid-thought reply to hold. Their design was live in session v-2joydc7 and still produced the filler the owner complained about ('Take your time, I'm here.', 13:12). Their proof e-fixes/proof/proof.mjs now fails 3 of 23, all the voice-line cases (4: fast reply held then released by /floor done; smart after done; the follow-on count) - superseded by design, not broken: the floor verb still releases a held reply for any line that reached the fast one. My sessions-test: 16/16 on the merged code.
decision.alternative: let /floor done also release held thoughts: rejected, it fires at 1.5 s, the gap the owner's mid-thought pauses already cross
